description: Southern Buttermilk Fried Chicken is an iconic American dish featuring tender chicken marinated in tangy buttermilk, then coated in seasoned flour and deep-fried to golden perfection. The buttermilk tenderizes the meat and helps create an incredibly crispy, flavorful crust. This classic comfort food is a staple in Southern cuisine, beloved for its juicy interior and satisfying crunch.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine buttermilk and hot sauce (if using). Add the chicken pieces, ensuring they are fully submerged. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the buttermilk to tenderize the chicken.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dredging Mixture
instructions.text: In a shallow dish or large resealable bag, whisk together the flour, cornstarch, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to ensure all spices are evenly distributed.

instructions.title: Dredge the Chicken
instructions.text: Remove the chicken pieces from the buttermilk, allowing any excess to drip off but do not rinse. One piece at a time, dredge the chicken thoroughly in the seasoned flour mixture, pressing firmly to ensure a thick, even coating. Place the coated chicken on a wire rack set over a baking sheet and let it rest for 15-20 minutes. This helps the coating adhere better.

instructions.title: Heat the Oil
instructions.text: Pour the vegetable or peanut oil into a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, filling it about 3-4 inches deep. Heat the oil over medium-high heat until it reaches 350-375F (175-190C). Use a deep-fry thermometer to monitor the temperature accurately.

instructions.title: Fry the Chicken
instructions.text: Carefully place 2-3 pieces of chicken into the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot. Fry the chicken for about 6-8 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through. Breasts and wings may cook faster than thighs and drumsticks. The internal temperature should reach 165F (74C).

instructions.title: Drain and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the chicken from the oil and place it on a clean wire rack set over a baking sheet lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil. Season lightly with a pinch of salt while still hot. Repeat with remaining chicken pieces, ensuring the oil temperature returns to 350-375F (175-190C) between batches. Serve immediately.

tips: For truly authentic Southern flavor, marinate the chicken for a full 24 hours. This maximizes tenderness and allows the flavors to deeply penetrate the meat.
Do not overcrowd the frying pot. Frying too many pieces at once will lower the oil temperature, resulting in greasy chicken with a less crispy crust.
Maintain a consistent oil temperature between 350-375F (175-190C). Use a thermometer and adjust heat as needed; too low results in oily chicken, too high burns the exterior before the interior cooks.
